passages.text: Please read this Action for Heroes Guide BEFORE you begin to read the storybook with the children and continue to use its advice after you finish.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: The storybook, “My Hero is You, How kids can fight COVID-19!”

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: , explains how children can protect themselves, their families and friends from the coronavirus and how to manage difficult emotions when confronted with our new and rapidly changing reality.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: You can read and download this book for free on the IASC website.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: It has been translated into 125+ languages and multi¬media adaptations have been made.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Links to these resources are available at the end of this guide.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: It is recommended that adults read the storybook WITH the children.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: As they read the storybook, this Guide directs adults about how to have Heart-to-Heart CHATS with children and educate them about the coronavirus and COVID-19.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: It explains how adults can create safe spaces for children to openly share their feelings, including their fears and worries about the coronavirus and frustrations at their changed daily lives.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: The Guide also directs adults about how to promote positive actions that children can take to protect themselves and others.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: It is best when children are informed with accurate information about the coronavirus and its risks and how to prevent the COVID-19 infectious disease by adults who are known to them and trusted like parents, caregivers and teachers.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: The language used to explain the facts can be simple and direct and modified to the age of the children.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Children who are not well informed are at risk of not taking precautions seriously and putting themselves and others at risk of infection.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Also, poorly informed children can become unnecessarily anxious because they feel adults are hiding the truth from them.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Even from a young age, children are aware of changes around them, so it is important to speak with even young children about what is going on.

passages.heading: Introduction
passages.text: Since the storybook encourages children to be heroes and take an active role in prevention, it is important for adults to balance an explanation of the problems and risks of the coronavirus with clear descriptions about how adults will protect the children and what the children can do to prevent infection and protect themselves and others.

passages.heading: When preparing to read with children, please remember:
passages.text: When preparing to read with children, please remember:

passages.text: The story can be read with one or more children.

passages.heading: When preparing to read with children, please remember:
passages.text: An adult or an older child can read page by page.

passages.heading: When preparing to read with children, please remember:
passages.text: It is best to read slowly and tell the story with a bit of drama.

passages.heading: When preparing to read with children, please remember:
passages.text: The adults and children want to see the pictures, so sit close, but not too close together, to allow for proper physical distancing, and arrange the seating so the children can easily see the pictures.

passages.heading: When preparing to read with children, please remember:
passages.text: Try to sit in a quiet space where you can avoid interruptions.

passages.heading: When preparing to read with children, please remember:
passages.text: When reading with a group of children, adults are responsible to ensure that all of the children have the chance to safely share their thoughts and feelings during the CHATs.

passages.heading: When preparing to read with children, please remember:
passages.text: The CHATs are good opportunities for adults to teach children effective ways to manage their fears and stressful situations.

passages.heading: Sharing information:
passages.text: Sharing information:

passages.heading: Sharing information:
passages.text: First, adults need to be well informed so that during a CHAT they share accurate information with children.

passages.heading: Sharing information:
passages.text: Remember, children have some awareness about the coronavirus since they are keen listeners and at every age hear adults talking and feel their emotional cues.

passages.heading: Sharing information:
passages.text: Adults can answer children’s questions honestly to ensure that they have a clear understanding of the coronavirus and its risks.

passages.heading: Sharing information:
passages.text: The answers can be scary, so adults can use the CHATs to reassure children and explain the actions they as adults and the children can take to keep safe.

passages.heading: Sharing information:
passages.text: For children feeling safe not only comes from knowing adults are there to care for them, feeling safe also comes from learning ways they can feel empowered or strong enough to be heroes and take actions to protect themselves and those they love.

passages.heading: Sharing information:
passages.text: The second direction for CHATs encourages adults to take the time to listen and hear what children feel and think about today’s changed life.

passages.text: Hearing children:

passages.heading: Hearing children:
passages.text: To encourage children to chat freely adults will:

passages.heading: Hearing children:
passages.text: Sincerely take the time to show their interest in what the children think and feel.

passages.heading: Hearing children:
passages.text: Listen and be patient as children talk and hear what children say and feel.

passages.heading: Hearing children:
passages.text: Talk with the children.

passages.heading: Hearing children:
passages.text: Do not talk at them or to them.

passages.heading: Hearing children:
passages.text: Talk with them.

passages.heading: Hearing children:
passages.text: Ask questions to show interest and understand the children’s thoughts and feelings.

passages.heading: Hearing children:
passages.text: Reflect on what the children say to have two-way discussions.

passages.heading: Hearing children:
passages.text: Educate children and honestly reassure them about the present situation.

passages.heading: Hearing children:
passages.text: Offer realistic protection to children.

passages.heading: Hearing children:
passages.text: Offer support and love to the children.

passages.heading: Hearing children:
passages.text: In a group reading, give equal opportunity for children to speak when they want.

passages.heading: Hearing children:
passages.text: Encourage children to listen and respond to each other in respectful ways.

passages.text: A Dad and his 10 years old son, Salem are reading the storybook together.

passages.text: At CHAT 2 Dad wants to talk with Salem about his feelings regarding the coronavirus.

passages.text: Some nights it’s hard to fall asleep.

passages.heading: Example of a CHAT that HEARs the child:
passages.text: I worry I won’t wake up.

passages.heading: Example of a CHAT that HEARs the child:
passages.text: Dad: I am sorry you worry at night.

passages.heading: Example of a CHAT that HEARs the child:
passages.text: I didn’t know you felt like this.

passages.heading: Example of a CHAT that HEARs the child:
passages.text: What makes you worry that you won’t wake up?

passages.text: Salem: I heard some children died from Corona.

passages.heading: Example of a CHAT that HEARs the child:
passages.text: I don’t know why they died but I heard someone say this.

passages.text: If I get the virus will I die?

passages.text: Honest response to fact.

passages.text: Dad: A very small number of children around the world got very sick from the virus and died.

passages.heading: Example of a CHAT that HEARs the child:
passages.text: It is very rare.

passages.heading: Example of a CHAT that HEARs the child:
passages.text: You are healthy and most of these children had other health problems in addition to the virus.

passages.heading: Example of a CHAT that HEARs the child:
passages.text: Salem: So, I won’t die if I get the virus?

passages.heading: Example of a CHAT that HEARs the child:
passages.text: Dad: It is very unlikely that you will die if you get the virus.

passages.heading: Example of a CHAT that HEARs the child:
passages.text: Most often children do not get seriously ill and die.

passages.heading: Example of a CHAT that HEARs the child:
passages.text: Salem: That’s good to know.

passages.heading: Example of a CHAT that HEARs the child:
passages.text: When you worry at night, let’s agree on what we can do to help you feel safe and sleep.

passages.heading: Example of a CHAT that HEARs the child:
passages.text: Salem’s Dad listened and encouraged Salem to share his feelings.

passages.heading: Example of a CHAT that HEARs the child:
passages.text: He responded with kindness, support and accurate information.

passages.heading: Example of a CHAT that HEARs the child:
passages.text: He offered to help Salem to find ways to feel safe at night.

passages.heading: Example of a CHAT that HEARs the child:
passages.text: Salem responded positively and was encouraged to continue to CHAT.

passages.text: Whether we are chatting with one child or a group of children, in each CHAT adults will focus on essential messages and keep the CHATs brief to avoid losing the intensity of reading the story.

passages.heading: Length of CHAT
passages.text: Length of CHAT

passages.heading: Length of CHAT
passages.text: We want to give opportunities for all children to share their ideas and feelings.

passages.heading: Length of CHAT
passages.text: However, some children like to talk, some rarely want to talk and some talk too much.

passages.heading: Length of CHAT
passages.text: Adults will need to control the length of each CHAT.

passages.heading: Length of CHAT
passages.text: If a child is talking a lot, adults listen and remind them we want to go back to the story and arrange to talk more after they finish reading the story.

passages.heading: Length of CHAT
passages.text: Some children do not feel comfortable to speak.

passages.heading: Length of CHAT
passages.text: Best not to push them.

passages.heading: Length of CHAT
passages.text: This is story time and children can listen and learn and not everyone needs to talk.

passages.heading: Unique CHATS
passages.text: CHATs vary by cultures and the personalities and the relationship of the adults and children.

passages.heading: Unique CHATS
passages.text: A CHAT with a teacher will be different than a CHAT with a parent.

passages.heading: Unique CHATS
passages.text: However, the purpose of the CHATS are always the same.

passages.heading: Unique CHATS
passages.text: The CHAT is a safe place for children to share their thoughts and feelings, to learn facts about the coronavirus, and understand how children can take responsible action to protect themselves and others.

passages.heading: ADULTS BENEFIT FROM LISTENING TO CHILDREN
passages.text: It is best not to offend them and remind them that at their young age it is unlikely they know everything.

passages.text: However, we also want them to accept their limitations, so they know it is okay when they do not know, okay to sometimes have feelings like being unsure or anxious, and okay to ask for help.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: Start your chats with children by sharing clear factual information about the coronavirus and Covid-19.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: Children can only learn how to protect themselves if they fully understand the virus and its risks.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: Adults ask open questions to invite children to talk about what they know.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: As the children speak, and they recognize adults are listening, they can feel comfortable to continue to share their ideas, thoughts and feelings.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: HOW FAR IS FAR ENOUGH?

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: Different country health systems recommend 1-2 meters for “social” or “physical” distancing.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: Please check what is recommended in your country and use this with the children.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: To be sure children understand how big is the distance you can pace the distance or use a ruler, a piece of string or have the children lie on the floor to measure 1 or 2 meters.

passages.text: WORLD FAMOUS SCIENTISTS STILL LEARNING ABOUT CORONAVIRUS

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: We are all still learning about this new coronavirus.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: Scientists do not have all the answers.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: Adults do not have all the answers.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: Yet, children are asking questions and adults must do their best to answer as well as let children know we are all still learning.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: If children challenge the risks to them as children, adults can respond with, “You are right.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: Children do not often get seriously sick from the virus.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: BUT, some do and there are still risks.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: Many people, including children, can have the virus inside them and pass it to others.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: Your little sister has a heart problem and if she gets the virus it can be serious because she has other health problems.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: And, Grandma and Grandpa need to avoid getting the virus because older people can become very sick and even die from the virus.”

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: Children need to be part of helping to protect people and prevent them from getting the virus.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: If Sara asked, “I don’t want to get anyone sick.

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: How do I know if I have the virus inside me?”

passages.heading: CHILDREN NEED TO KNOW THE FACTS ABOUT COVID-19
passages.text: Sara’s Mum can answer, “Most often you don’t know because you feel fine.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: The coronavirus is causing a disease called COVID-19.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: It is a new virus and the disease is contagious - that means it passes from one person to another.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: The disease became a global pandemic since it spread to countries around the world.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: The coronavirus moves from one person to another through droplets that come from the mouth or nose of an infected person who talks, laughs, cries, coughs or sneezes.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: These droplets fly into the air and can land in the mouths or noses of people close-by.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: The droplets can also land on a table, chair or other surface and we if we touch it and touch our eyes, nose or mouth we can get infected.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: You need to tell me right away if you or anyone you know has any of the virus symptoms like headache, cough, sneezing, body aches, fever and loss of sense of smell and/or taste.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: We need to be extra careful since even having one symptom can mean you are infected and can pass the virus to others.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: The good news is that most people only get mildly sick.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: However, even if they feel better in a few days they might still be contagious and need to stay home and keep away from everyone until their doctors say they are no longer contagious.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: It’s a sneaky virus because many people have the virus but feel fine.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: They can still give it to someone else even if they don’t mean to do it.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: I know it all sounds scary.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: That’s why we are talking and reading this book.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: I am doing everything I can to keep us healthy.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: I want to be sure you know how to protect yourself and not get the virus!

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: I know you want to go out to play with your friends.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: But, we must go out safely.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: To avoid the droplets from someone who is infected, it is best to wear a mask.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: We also need to physically distance to avoid the droplets so we must stay at least 1 meter away from another person.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: The best protection is washing with soap and water so we will clean our hands more than ever.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: If we avoid touching our eyes, nose and mouth, even if we touch the virus we can avoid bringing it into our body.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: All over the world, people, like us, are reading this storybook and learning how to prevent the spread of the virus.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: Children ask questions and the adults answer their questions.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 1 Staying healthy
passages.text: The virus has turned our world upside down.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: ADULTS AND CHILDREN FEEL STRESSED

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: Today’s times are stressful for everyone in every country in every city on every street across the world.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: It is unrealistic to imagine that adults or children can be fully rid of all our stress.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: It is more realistic to learn to manage or cope with our stress.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: It is honest to acknowledge that we all feel stressed - adults and children - and CHAT with the children about realistic ways they can cope that fit their ages, cultures and environments.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: Of course, you as adults, also feel stress.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: Your children will see and feel your stress and often copy you.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: A girl seems sad and stressed

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: BE HONEST AND SHARE YOUR STRESS

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: Finding ways to cope with your own stress is important for your peace of mind and is an example your children can copy for how they can cope with their stress.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: UNDERSTANDING CHILDREN’S

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: STRESS

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: Adults need to assist children to find ways they can cope with their feelings of stress.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: Important to be patient and try to understand their reasons for feeling this stress.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: It is good to praise the children for their efforts to cope and remain patient since the stress is ongoing and won’t just disappear.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: A man is sitting with the child and cuddling him.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: BREATHING EXERCISE HELP

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: Adults can teach children how to use breathing exercises to help them relax.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: Good for adults to try the exercises themselves first so they feel the benefit and then teach the children.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: When adults teach the breathing exercises they should speak slowly and in a calm, low voice.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: If children breathe too fast, it will not be helpful.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: If children breath too slowly, they will be uncomfortable.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: Adults can encourage children to continue to use the breathing exercises to help them relax whenever they feel scared.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: Some children might say, “The breathing did nothing.”

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: Adults can encourage these children to try it at times when they really feel scared and then check if it helps.

passages.heading: MANAGING OUR STRESS
passages.text: Adults can also encourage children to think of others ways to relax.

passages.text: I have some more ideas about what to do when we get scared.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 3 Coping with stress
passages.text: First, it is good to share and tell me or another adult when you feel scared.

passages.text: We can always CHAT, not only today when we read the storybook.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 3 Coping with stress
passages.text: I hope when you feel scared you tell me and together, we can find ways to help you to relax.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 3 Coping with stress
passages.text: Chatting can help us to relax.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 3 Coping with stress
passages.text: “A problem shared is a problem halved.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 3 Coping with stress
passages.text: There are lots of ways to relax.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 3 Coping with stress
passages.text: To relax, we can play sports, run, dance, sing or pray.

passages.text: Ario says when he wants to relax he breathes slowly and out comes fire.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 3 Coping with stress

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 3 Coping with stress
passages.text: Breathing slowly and deeply can help us to relax.

passages.text: We breathe in slowly and as we breathe in we count in our heads 1-2-3-4-5.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 3 Coping with stress
passages.text: And, slowly we release the breath and count in our heads 1-2-3-4-5.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: HOW CAN CHILDREN FEEL SAFE?

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: With the challenges of COVID-19, all children need support.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: Feelings of safety come from adults like moms, dads, grandparents, nannies, teachers and religious leaders.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: Where children live or the amount of money, toys, food or clothes that adults give are not what helps children feel safe.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: Feelings of safety come from the heart.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: Adults offering sincere, compassionate support is what makes children feel safe.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: Feeling safe will allow the children to cope with the challenges that now surround them.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: CHATTING WITH A CHILD WITH A PROBLEM

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: Teachers or other adults reading the story to a group, need to take care in speaking with children about their problems in front of other children.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: If a child mentions a specific personal problem during the group reading, it is best to ask the child to talk about it with you after the reading.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: Always best to sit with the child separately to talk about how this child can feel safe.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: It is particularly important to listen when a child says, “I never feel safe.”It could take a long time to discuss this and understand why and what to do.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: Whether you are the child’s parent or teacher, your response is similar.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: Since you are in the middle of reading a storybook, it is probably best to say to the child, “I am sorry to hear this.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: I would like to talk to you more about why you feel this way and what I can do to help.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: Let’s read the story now and right after we can talk about it.”

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: Then, be sure, to make time to talk to this child about the fears and find ways for this child to feel safe.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: GIVING HUGS?

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: Depending on the relationship with the child, we have different way to physically show support.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: Parents or caregivers can give their children lots of hugs during and after the story to help them feel safe.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: At school, with children wearing masks it is hard to see their emotions so we need to ask how they feel since we cannot rely on body language.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: Teachers cannot hug children freely so they need to find the ways that are best in their culture to show their support.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: They can say to the children, “Let’s all give ourselves a hug.”

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: Teachers can hugs themselves and teach the children how to wrap their arms around themselves and give themselves a hug.

passages.heading: FEELING SAFE COMES FROM THE HEART
passages.text: Adults can remind children that giving themselves a hug when they feel scared or sad can be helpful at any time.

passages.text: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe

passages.text: CHAT 4

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Let’s CHAT

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Sara and Salem talked about how their grandparents make them feel “safe”.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Living with the coronavirus has everyone a bit scared.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Feeling safe makes us take a big deep sigh of relief and feel the comfort of being hugged.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Even if no one touched us, feeling safe, lets us feel hugged.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: There are many ways to feel safe.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: For some kids, seeing their Mum smile at them during a hard time might let them feel safe.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: For other kids, staying at home and playing games with their brothers and sisters and not being teased helps them feel safe.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Or, having their Dad join their kid games can make them feel safe.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Sara and Salem

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: ASK the children

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Who makes you feel safe and what is it they say or do that gives you a feeling of safety?

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Children might say:

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: “My Dad has no work.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: He stays at home all day now.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: He always looks miserable.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Yesterday, we all put on masks and went outside.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: We just ran and tried to catch each other but did not touch.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Playing with my Dad made me feel safe.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: “Eating dinner with my family makes me feel safe.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: “Sitting around a campfire with the family all together makes me feel safe.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Let’s CHAT

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: The coronavirus makes us worry about another kind of safety.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: We worry about staying healthy and keep our bodies safe from catching COVID-19.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Ario praised Sasha because she is staying home.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Her Dad is sick with COVID-19 and he is contagious and could give COVID-19 to other people, so he is self-isolating and staying in his bedroom away from other people.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Sasha is picking flowers and does not feel sick, but she lived in the same house with her Dad before he got sick.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Sometimes people can have the virus inside their bodies and feel fine but can still be contagious.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Sasha is a hero because she is staying home and not taking any chances that she might have the virus and could make someone else sick.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Sasha and her Dad are staying home and keeping other people safe from getting sick.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Being in self-isolation is lonely.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: There are many things Sasha could do to bring a smile to her Dad.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: It doesn’t matter whether Sasha is in a wheelchair or walking or from our same country or from another, we all can bring a smile to someone we love.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: This is especially important when the person we love has a problem.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: As example, Sasha could sing outside her Dad’s window.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: ASK the children

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: What other ways can Sasha help her Dad smile while he is sick?

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Children could say:

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: “Sasha could draw pictures and push them under the door of his room.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: “Sasha could put flowers on the tray her Dad gets for his food.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: “She could chat to her Dad outside his door.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: ASK the children

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Let’s pretend we are Sasha’s father.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: What does Sasha’s father say to Sasha after she sings to him to let her know how he feels about her singing?

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Children might say that Sasha’s father could say:

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: “Your singing made me feel better.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: “Your singing made me happy.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Thanks.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: I love you.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Let’s CHAT

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: Feeling safe and closely connected to other people during COVID-19 is important.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 4 Keeping each other safe
passages.text: We can feel hugged if every day we remember to do something for each other that brings us a smile and makes us feel safe.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: HOUR AFTER HOUR FAMILIES AT HOME

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: Before COVID-19, we wished for days when families could get extra time together.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: We welcomed days when Dads and Mums had no work or other things to do and children had no school and we could spend our days together.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: With COVID-19, too much of that wish came true.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: Now, stuck together day after day, we often wish for more to do.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: Yet, it seems we need to get used to being at home and surrounded by family more.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: Rather than wake up every morning dreading the day, it seems best to find new ways to improve being home.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: AGREE ON A DAILY ROUTINE

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: A boy sleeping in a blanket. The sun is shining brightly outside the window of his room.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: Families need routines for a set time to wake up - eat - go to sleep.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: It is good for everyone to have chores and share responsibilities for cooking and cleaning.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: Clear plans for how adults and children have space to do schoolwork or adult work at home are critical.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: What to do for fun also takes some family planning since the usual home activities may have become boring.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: It’s also not healthy for families to just sit around so exercise and fresh air needs to be part of a plan.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: And, like Sasha said, a bit of time alone and space for oneself, feels good.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: TALK IT OUT

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: Continaul family togetherness can lead to short tempers and disagreements.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: It is best for adults to agree with children on a few treasured ways to manage problems.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: As example, when a disagreement becomes tense and words and actions are making it worse it is best to separate.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: Always best to avoid saying or doing things in the heat of the angry moment you will later regret.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: Moving to a separate space or corner and using slow breathing to relax and cool down is helpful.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: A man trying to resolve a disagreement among children. His left arm is around the shoulders of the girl child and right around the shoulders of boy child.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: It can be useful to involve a third party to mediate and help to solve the issues.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: Then, you can return to be together after you agree you are cool enough to talk.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: Problems are best solved with talk!

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: Each person talks - one by one - and everyone listens.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: The goal is to solve the problems, so we need to stay positive and not blame or accuse the other or keep a grudge.

passages.heading: FAMILIES FIGHT COVID-19 TOGETHER
passages.text: Learning to compromise, where each person feels heard leads to solving problems together and giving all people some of what they want.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: CHAT 5

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: Let’s CHAT

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: Being home together all the time, is both wonderful and difficult.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: First, let’s talk about what’s wonderful.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: (Parents shares first, saying what’s wonderful for them.)

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: A man and a women

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: ASK the children

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: What’s wonderful for you about us being home together more than ever

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: Children might say:

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: “It’s wonderful doing my schoolwork with you.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: It’s only you and me so I can understand everything.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: “It’s wonderful to have Dad home and not at work all the time.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: “It’s wonderful to stay up late together every night.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: Salem and Sasha talked about family fights.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: Sometimes families fight when they get angry or frustrated with each other.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: Other times, they end up fighting when they get tired or bored or just need some time alone.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: Sasha gave some good advice.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: She said, the best way to solve problems in her family is to be “extra patient, and extra understanding, and even quicker to say I’m sorry.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: I like Sasha’s advice for fixing family fights.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: Family fighting always feels bad.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: We can think together about ways to fix family fights.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: I have one idea.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: When we feel angry or frustrated, we move away from each other.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: We find a separate room or corner to be in and we say, “Please, I need space” and everyone respects this.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: After about 10 minutes, the fighters check, “Are you ready to talk?”.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: They wait enough time until both are cool and ready to talk.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: The fighters then sit together and talk.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: Each person talks - one by one - and everyone listens.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: The goal is to solve the problems, so we need to stay positive and not blame or accuse each other.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: Each person will have to give the other some of what they want to solve the problem.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: If we stay calm and talk, maybe we can avoid the fight.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: ASK the children

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: What other ideas do you have to fix our problems to avoid a fight?

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: Children might say:

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: “I like your idea.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: No one listens to me when I get angry.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: It makes me angrier.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: “My Teacher needs to listen to all sides of a fight not just one kid”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: “My Mom needs to listen to me when I get angry.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: A child

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: Let’s CHAT

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: Sasha’s advice is also good in school.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: She said, the best way to solve problems is to be “extra patient, and extra understanding, and even quicker to say I’m sorry.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: Sometimes children fight in school.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: It is best if we take Sasha’s advice and avoid fights by being patient and understanding of each other.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: Let’s remember to listen when someone is angry to understand why.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 5 Solving problems
passages.text: If it is your fault, say “I’m sorry.”

passages.text: COVID-19 has no boundaries.

passages.text: Adults can teach children about why Leila and other children live in camps.

passages.heading: COVID-19 HAS NO BOUNDARIES
passages.text: Dangerous situations where people are fighting, or there is not enough food or there was a flood or a fire or another disaster, can cause people to move into a camp.

passages.heading: COVID-19 HAS NO BOUNDARIES
passages.text: Some people have to leave their homes and go to a camp in another country to live safely.

passages.heading: COVID-19 HAS NO BOUNDARIES
passages.text: While others, can live safely in a camp in their own country.

passages.heading: COVID-19 HAS NO BOUNDARIES
passages.text: Most hope to return to their own homes someday but this is not always possible.

passages.heading: COVID-19 HAS NO BOUNDARIES
passages.text: In these camps, people have greater risks to get infected by Covid-19.

passages.heading: COVID-19 HAS NO BOUNDARIES
passages.text: It is difficult for children to follow the rules that can protect them if they live in crowded conditions with shortages of water and soap.

passages.heading: COVID-19 HAS NO BOUNDARIES
passages.text: In these situations, children become heroes by finding creative ways to stay safe from the virus.

passages.heading: COVID-19 HAS NO BOUNDARIES
passages.text: They can share information about practical ways to be safe that fit camp life to help protect others.

passages.heading: COVID-19 HAS NO BOUNDARIES

passages.heading: HOW TO DEAL WITH A BROKEN HEART?
passages.text: This is the most challenging CHAT.

passages.heading: HOW TO DEAL WITH A BROKEN HEART?
passages.text: Adults have the responsibility to protect children, keep them safe and shield them the best they can from heartache.

passages.heading: HOW TO DEAL WITH A BROKEN HEART?
passages.text: Sadly, this is not always possible.

passages.heading: HOW TO DEAL WITH A BROKEN HEART?
passages.text: Life’s realities force adults to prepare children for how to live even when their hearts ache.

passages.heading: HOW TO DEAL WITH A BROKEN HEART?
passages.text: Adults will leave children unprepared and alone if they skip this CHAT and avoid leading them safely through reality.

passages.heading: HOW TO DEAL WITH A BROKEN HEART?

passages.heading: HOW TO DEAL WITH A BROKEN HEART?

passages.heading: HOW TO DEAL WITH A BROKEN HEART?
passages.text: As hard as it is, adults need to talk with children about living with death.

passages.heading: HOW TO DEAL WITH A BROKEN HEART?
passages.text: For some people, faith and spirituality is important to help children to live with death.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: Leila asked a question that is difficult to answer.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: She asked, “Is it true some people die from the coronavirus.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: Ario answered Leila’s questions, “Yes, some people die from Covid-19.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: I prefer that your life never includes any heartache.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: I, along with your whole family and everyone who loves you, will do everything we can to protect you.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: Sadly, death is a part of life and affects all of us.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: I am unable to protect you from experiencing death.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: This is one of the realities in all our lives that causes us heartache.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: Our lives take many turns and twists and I am here to help you to manage them.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: Yes, some people do die from COVID-19.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: Most often they are people who are older or people who are already sick with another disease.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: We must be extra careful to protect these people from getting infected.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: Sometimes, mums, dads or big brothers, sisters or even children die from COVID-19.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: It does not happen often, but it can happen.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: Even when we are careful, sometimes people still get sick and die.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: No one is to blame.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: It is no one’s fault.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: Having people we love die is something we will all experience at some time in our lives.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: When someone dies, it really helps to talk about how we feel to someone who cares about us.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: We can hug each other.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: We can share the stories of our memories about the people who died.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: When people die, we miss them.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: By sharing memories when we were happy together, we can remember these people and keep them alive in our hearts.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: Now, we will learn the way Ario suggested to Sara, Salem and Leila manage their feelings when they feel sad or scared or unsafe.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: Ario suggested they imagine inside their minds the look, feel, smell of a place that once made them happy.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: Ario thought that imaging a guest to go with you to this place could help you feel better.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: Your guest can be anyone you choose.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: So, think of who you want to take to that place with you.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: I suggest that we add a few deep breathes to all this imagining like we learned earlier to relax.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: This imagining can help us when we are sad or anxious.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: Right now, we are enjoying a story and feel good.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: So, let me remind you of the creepy coronavirus with all its legs.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 7 Living with heartache
passages.text: That makes all of us a little scared.

passages.text: Now, imagine you bring your guest to that safe place with you.

passages.text: Remember, I am here to help keep you safe.

passages.heading: WHEN ARE WE SAFE FROM A PERSON WHO WAS INFECTED?
passages.text: WELCOME BACK AFTER COVID-19

passages.heading: WHEN ARE WE SAFE FROM A PERSON WHO WAS INFECTED?
passages.text: Some people catch the coronavirus and get sick and most get better.

passages.heading: WHEN ARE WE SAFE FROM A PERSON WHO WAS INFECTED?
passages.text: Once they are no longer contagious, they are no risk to anyone.

passages.heading: WHEN ARE WE SAFE FROM A PERSON WHO WAS INFECTED?
passages.text: Logically, we should be happy to see them, and eat, socialize, play together like before they were sick.

passages.heading: WHEN ARE WE SAFE FROM A PERSON WHO WAS INFECTED?
passages.text: Why doesn’t it always happen like that?

passages.heading: WHEN ARE WE SAFE FROM A PERSON WHO WAS INFECTED?
passages.text: Why are some people who had the coronavirus rejected by their friends, family and communities?

passages.heading: WHEN ARE WE SAFE FROM A PERSON WHO WAS INFECTED?
passages.text: A boy and a girl who have recovered from coronavirus are standing in a sad mood. Both are wearing a mask.

passages.heading: WHEN ARE WE SAFE FROM A PERSON WHO WAS INFECTED?
passages.text: FEAR SHOULD NOT BE STRONGER

passages.heading: WHEN ARE WE SAFE FROM A PERSON WHO WAS INFECTED?
passages.text: THAN SCIENCE

passages.heading: WHEN ARE WE SAFE FROM A PERSON WHO WAS INFECTED?
passages.text: Even though science teaches us that a person is now safe many people don’t want to take any chances, so they keep their distance.

passages.heading: WHEN ARE WE SAFE FROM A PERSON WHO WAS INFECTED?
passages.text: The people who were sick are sometimes rejected by others.

passages.heading: WHEN ARE WE SAFE FROM A PERSON WHO WAS INFECTED?
passages.text: People don’t want to be rejected so sometimes they pretend to be well and continue to work, go to school and socialize even when they are sick with COVID-19.

passages.heading: WHEN ARE WE SAFE FROM A PERSON WHO WAS INFECTED?
passages.text: Others need to work to feed their families so decide to work even though they know they are sick.

passages.heading: WHEN ARE WE SAFE FROM A PERSON WHO WAS INFECTED?
passages.text: Self-isolating when you are sick is helping to stop the spread of the virus.

passages.heading: WHEN ARE WE SAFE FROM A PERSON WHO WAS INFECTED?
passages.text: Children can be heroes and learn to be responsible citizens by saying when they are sick so they can get the care they need.

passages.heading: WHEN ARE WE SAFE FROM A PERSON WHO WAS INFECTED?
passages.text: Children can learn to love and care for people at a distance when they are sick and be ready to accept their friends and family back into their lives just as soon as they are not contagious.

passages.heading: WHEN ARE WE SAFE FROM A PERSON WHO WAS INFECTED?

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Let’s CHAT Feeling safe and cared for Sara, Salem and Leila circle the world with Ario.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Next stop, Ario introduces them to Kim who explains all about how he felt when he was sick with COVID-19.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: ASK the children

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: My first thought is, “I’m glad I wasn’t there when Kim got sick.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Why would I think that?”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: A man and a woman wearing a face mask

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Children might respond:

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: “The coronavirus can crawl from Kim to you and you don’t want to be sick and die.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: “I’m also glad I’m not there.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: “No one wants to be near anyone who was sick with COVID-19.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: We know the coronavirus is sneaky.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: We don’t see it as it passes from one person to another with ease.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: This virus does not infect all people the same.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Some people get very sick and some less sick.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Sometimes, we can’t tell that people have the virus.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Not everyone who gets sick tells other people they are sick.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: They keep it a secret.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Sometimes people are rejected after they were sick, so they keep it a secret because they don’t want to lose their friends.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: To keep everyone protected from the coronavirus it is important that everyone says, “I feel sick.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: I need your help,” immediately when they are sick.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: ASK children

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: What can we do to encourage everyone to speak out immediately when they are sick?

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Children might respond:

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: “We can let them know we won’t reject them.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: “We offer them help, like buying them food, when they are sick.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: It is a big relief that the coronavirus doesn’t stay in a person forever.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: When they are no longer contagious, we have no worries since we will not get the coronavirus from them.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: They are the same person as before they got sick.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: It is safe to talk and play and be together.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: People will feel safe to say, “I am sick.” when they know they will get our support.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: They are many kind safe ways we can show our support.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Adults can help by delivering them food and medicine and offering to run their errands.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Adults and children can call them on the phone and give them our care.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Children can copy Leila and sing at their windows.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Most important, is to remember to care for those who are sick - especially if they are older or alone.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Back to our story, it is almost the end.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Ario puts Sara back into her bed.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Her journey around the world has ended.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: When Sara began her journey, she was scared and felt the coronavirus had stolen her life.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: She wanted to be a hero and protect herself and tell children all over the world how to be safe.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: When she went to sleep, she did not know how to do this.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: As Ario says goodbye, Sara tells him, “You are my hero.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: I imagine Ario smiled when he said, “You are my hero too, Sara.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: ASK the children

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: What did Ario and Sara do that makes them both heroes?

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Children might say:

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: “They told children all over the world how to be safe and avoid catching the coronavirus.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Let’s CHAT

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: They were heroes because they went around the world and made sure that all children knew how to protect themselves from being infected by the coronavirus.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: ASK the children

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: What did all the children learn to do to be protected?

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Children might say:

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: “To wash our hands with soap.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: “Stay home.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: “If I go outside to play, then don’t touch my eyes or nose until I wash my hands.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: “When I am outside of the house wear a mask.”

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Let’s CHAT

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: It is important to remember all these rules of protection to avoid getting infected with the coronavirus:

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Wash your hands with soap many times a day

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Don’t touch your eyes or nose until you wash your hands

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Stay home or close to home if you go out to play.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Avoid big groups of people.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Wear a mask outside of the house

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: When outside of the house, keep a safe physical distance.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: When you return to school, follow school rules to stay safe.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: If you do get the virus or you have symptoms and might have the coronavirus, be a hero, be responsible.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Immediately, tell those people close to you so you can keep them safe and not infect them.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: When you know people are sick, offer your kind support.

passages.heading: KEY MESSAGE 8 Being a responsible citizen of the world
passages.text: Lastly, when they are healthy again, be there just as you were before they got sick.
